subject: Question about least square demo for rmr2

messages.author: 214e28117896a7a6
messages.subject: Question about least square demo for rmr2
parts:
Hello RHadoop group,
 
I have just managed to install RHadoop and have got everything running.
So I am rather new to this mapreduce topic.
 
My question is about the least square demo on https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/rmr2/blob/master/docs/tutorial.md 
 
I have tried to calculate the XtX with and without the "reduce=Sum" in the mapreduce function and the results were exactly the same, which were equal to t(X) %*% X.
If the big matrix X is splitted into multiple chunks, shouldn't I get a list of multiple cross-product-matrices when I omit the reduce?
Or did I understand something wrong?
 
Thank you very much for your help!

messages.author: 63023c771a070260
messages.subject: Re: Question about least square demo for rmr2
parts:
Maybe your data size is less than the chunk size. If you want to see the chunking behavior at a small scale, which is often helpful for debugging, you can call rmr.options(keyval.lenght = 10) or something small. It will degrade performance, so go back to higher values for larger runs


Antonio

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#1116] Re: Question about least square demo for rmr2
parts:
Hello Antonio,
thank you very much for your test case, which is very helpful indeed.
I did get a list of 8 matrices and I think I figured out what my problem was:
I calculated a
XtX_2 <- values(from.dfs(mapreduce(~~~)))[[1]]
without the reduce. In this case I could of course only get one matrix returned due to the "[[1]]" that I copied and pasted. But then I somehow confounded this matrix with the original XtX and thought they were the same...my bad
Now I get with
XtX_2 <- values(from.dfs(mapreduce(~~~)))
a list of 2 matrices and Reduce('+', XtX_2) gives me the original XtX.
So from this mistake and your help I did learn something about mapreduce.:)
Thank you very much!
P.S.
One more thing - I tried verifying the result with lm(y ~ X) and saw it is not the same as that from solve(XtX, Xty). But when I add a column of 1 to the left of X I could get same results.
